svg.text: BEST FOR: RULES VS. AI WORKFLOWS VS. AI AGENTS
FORMAT LINEAGE: Prem Natarajan (#13, 59 likes, 53 comments) & Chip Huyen
Traditional Automation vs. AI Workflows vs. Autonomous Agents: The 3-Column Decision Triptych
Don't use an autonomous agent for a deterministic cron job, and don't force an IF/THEN script to parse messy unstructured edge cases.
100% Application Code — every branch, retry, and field mapping
Schema validation, billing calculations, idempotency ledgers,
Brittle on unstructured inputs: fails immediately if a vendor
changes a PDF layout or column name.
Standard unit & integration tests (pytest / CI) with 100%
Cloud Workflows / Cloud Run ⇄ Temporal / Python / Airflow
USE FIRST whenever the rules and inputs are structured
Code-orchestrated steps with bounded LLM nodes
Code owns the control flow (the DAG); the LLM is called inside
specific nodes to parse, classify, or draft.
80% of enterprise AI: invoice extraction, support triage,
Node-level extraction errors — easily caught by Pydantic
validation and a single evaluator-optimizer retry.
Per-node golden dataset evals (Promptfoo / Vertex Eval) +
Vertex AI Pipelines / ADK Workflow ⇄ LangGraph DAG /
DEFAULT CHOICE when steps are known but data is messy
Model-directed planning & tool use inside a harness
The LLM dynamically decides which tools to call and how many
steps to take, bounded by a deterministic harness.
Compounding multi-step drift, retry storms, or tool misuse
unless gated by loop guards and sandboxes.
Google ADK + Cloud Run gVisor ⇄ OpenHands / LangGraph +
EARN THIS ONLY when the step sequence cannot be predicted
THE DECISION RULE (PREM NATARAJAN & CHIP HUYEN):

Start at Column 01 (Code). Move to Column 02 (AI Workflow) when inputs are unstructured. Move to Column 03 (Agent) only when the path itself cannot be scripted — and wrap Column 03 in Column 01 gates.
Rule: The best production AI systems are hybrids — an Autonomous Agent (Col 3) running inside an AI Workflow (Col 2) guarded by Traditional Automation (Col 1).
